target.title: fix(firecrawl): require own legacy provider config entries
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Firecrawl legacy web config lookup used inherited `firecrawl` properties from `tools.web.search` and `tools.web.fetch` as if they were explicit user config entries. A prototype-provided nested provider config could override the normal env/default behavior.

### Why This Change Was Made

Use own-property checks for the legacy nested Firecrawl entries while preserving the existing plugin config precedence and resolver shape.

### User Impact

Firecrawl only consumes legacy web config when users actually define the `firecrawl` entry on that config object. Inherited entries are ignored, so unset config falls back to the existing env/default path.

### Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/firecrawl/src/config.own-entries.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/firecrawl/src/config.ts extensions/firecrawl/src/config.own-entries.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --threads=1 extensions/firecrawl/src/config.ts extensions/firecrawl/src/config.own-entries.test.ts`
- `env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u OPENAI_ORG_ID -u OPENAI_PROJECT_ID .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (exit 0, no findings)
